outcome: Central and peripheral hemodynamic indicators (heart rate, SDD, UI, SI, OPSS, CR, LVMI, RR, SpO2, hourly urine output)
Type of blood circulation (eukinetic vs hypokinetic)
cohort: The study included 127 pregnant women aged 23-34 years with obesity of varying severity at 36-38 weeks gestation, and 28 control pregnant women of the same age and gestational age with normal body weight.
finding: An increase in body mass index to 40 or more kg/m2 (morbid obesity of the III degree) contributed to the progression of signs of heart failure, characterized by hypokinetic circulation, significantly decreased cardiac output, increased heart rate, and high myocardial oxygen demand.
